camera.position: chest level just behind and beside Nora's right shoulder, looking past her toward a small fern clearing
camera.framing: Nora's shoulder, ponytail and three-quarter profile fill the right third of the foreground; one juvenile Triceratops stands in the left two thirds of the frame in the midground, about two meters beyond the mossy log; tall conifer trunks and morning haze behind

setting.location: Hell Creek floodplain forest, Montana, Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago, warm humid morning
elements: soft hazy morning sunlight slants in from the upper left between tall straight conifer trunks; the air is warm and humid with a light haze; no snow, no frost, no winter anywhere
the ground is damp dark soil covered with low ankle-high ferns; there is no grass lawn
one fallen moss-covered log lies across the right foreground from frame 0; it stays in that same spot for the whole clip
one dense waist-high clump of tall green fern fronds stands in the left midground from frame 0; its fronds stay rooted in place and only sway when the animal brushes past them

exactly one juvenile Triceratops is already standing behind the fern clump from frame 0: its head, frill and front half are visible above and between the fronds, its hind half hidden behind them; it stays the only animal in the whole clip, it never appears suddenly and never vanishes

the juvenile Triceratops is about as tall as a pony at the shoulder, with a heavy rounded body on four thick legs, pebbly olive-brown scaly skin with darker mottling, a short hooked parrot-like beak, one short nose horn, two short brow horns that curve slightly backward, and a bony neck frill with a scalloped edge; it is a dinosaur, never a rhinoceros, never a cow, never a lizard, with no fur and no feathers

timeline_action.0-3s: From frame 0 the Triceratops stands behind the fern clump. From the very first frame at second 0, Nora begins speaking immediately in a hushed, excited voice in three-quarter profile toward the lens. The Triceratops sniffs the air toward her.
timeline_action.3-7s: The Triceratops shifts its weight back (anticipation), then pops out from behind the fern clump with a crisp elastic rebound (pop in) and takes two slow, heavy steps forward, stopping about two meters from the log; its body rolls slightly with each step and settles when it stops.
timeline_action.7-10s: It lowers its head, tears one low fern frond with its beak and chews, then lifts its head and looks toward the lens as the clip ends. Nora finishes her line toward the lens by about second 9.
